name: Architectural visualisation and drawings
one_line: A commissioned or self-directed architectural visualisation record that joins a named building or scheme to scene/model sources, rendered views or competition boards, review and approval evidence, and any stated display or use conditions; construction issue sets and isolated property images remain elsewhere.

deterministic: a labelled architectural visualisation brief or commission naming a building or scheme, viewpoint or scene requirements, audience or use, requested render/board outputs, and a maker or approver role
a source-to-output packet in which a readable 3D scene/model or parametric source, linked materials/assets, camera/view definitions, render outputs and a manifest share an explicit scheme identifier
a review packet that identifies exact rendered views or board revisions, records comments or requested changes, and is followed by a revised render set or an approval naming the same views
an approval or use-rights record that names the exact render/board set, project or scheme, approver or commissioning party, and permitted display, publication, marketing, competition or planning use

a competition or planning presentation packet whose boards, stills or animations are joined to the underlying scene/model and a named submission or approval record; the presentation envelope itself may belong to a neighbouring domain
needs_llm: deciding whether the building or scheme named in a brief is the subject of the visualisation, the client, the site owner, a depicted precedent, or merely a reference

deciding whether a .skp, .blend, .3dm, .max, .rvt or IFC-like file is a visualisation scene, a construction/BIM authoring model, a survey/model import, or a code/engineering artifact; extension alone is insufficient
matching a model, texture pack, camera file and rendered stills when filenames differ but scene metadata, view labels, asset links and manifest references establish one source-to-output chain
separating a client approval of photorealistic views from approval of drawings, planning submission, construction issue, lease material, or a marketing listing
deciding whether a render is an authored project output, a downloaded reference, a portfolio case study, a photograph of a built site, or an image supplied by another party
deciding whether an approval or licence covers all views, only named images, a competition entry, a marketing campaign, or a time/territory-limited use
never_alone: a .skp, .blend, .3dm, .max, .rvt, .dwg, .fbx, .obj, .ifc, .png, .jpg, .tif or .mp4 extension; file format routes extraction and does not establish architectural visualisation
the words render, rendering, visualisation, visualization, CGI, architecture, building, house, scheme, flythrough, exterior, interior, final or approved in a filename
a building, architect, developer, client, studio, site or project name without labelled role-bearing text and a source-to-output or approval relationship
a single photorealistic image, screenshot, panorama or animation without authored source, brief, review, submission, or use-rights evidence
a title block, drawing number, revision table, issue status or transmittal; those are stronger evidence for construction_property.drawings-revisions than for this row
a version token, FINAL suffix, render timestamp, folder called Renders or a bounded export/download session
visual similarity, shared textures, a matching address, EXIF absence, or a public architecture image; each may describe reference or neighbouring material
an architect's author metadata, company PDF metadata, email domain, or a named planning authority without a role-bearing record
a generic review email, client comment, contract, invoice, planning application or marketing pack without exact view/model references

grouping_reasons: one building or scheme across brief, scene/model sources, linked assets, views, renders, boards and approval records
one view family when camera/view identifiers, source references and successive render outputs are explicit
one commission from requested visual purpose through review, approval and permitted-use record
one competition or planning image packet only when its visual assets can be joined to the underlying source and submission context
no group for an isolated render, downloaded reference, portfolio case study, construction issue set, survey capture, or property listing image

template.why: Empty by binding contract: the creative schema declares no field rows. The distinctive architecture-specific chain is a grouping and activation signal, not a permission to mint scheme, building, view, client or stage fields. If the creative proposals are later adopted, project should precede stage and artifact_type; view/camera, software, model format and use purpose remain values or retrieval metadata unless the schema is deliberately changed. Not time-first: request, model, render, review, approval and publication have different clocks.

collides_with.signal: Both may contain architectural PDFs, models and scheme names. A controlled title block, drawing-number register, issue status and transmittal identify a construction drawing set; this row requires the visualisation brief/source-to-render chain and view/use approval.

A commissioned render packet may be part of a broader client engagement. Client briefs, general feedback, scope, fees and ordinary delivery remain client-engagement; this row activates only when the architectural scene/model-to-render chain is independently evidenced.

Both contain marked-up PDFs, R2/R3 tokens and changed outputs. Generic review vocabulary is universal; this row requires the architecture-specific source/view/render object and does not turn a revision round into a domain.

A competition board or portfolio case study may depict the same renders. Career owns the capability presentation or submission record when sources and project workflow are absent; authored scene, renders and approval/use records remain creative when their making purpose is evidenced.

A flat render and a photograph can depict the same building. Camera capture metadata, event chronology and photographic provenance support photos; scene/model lineage and render approval support this row.

falls_through_to.why: A durable brief, board, model or approval record without a recoverable architectural visualisation chain remains a standalone record.
Ambiguous model/render packets, unjoined revisions and unlabeled approvals require review rather than inference from architecture vocabulary.
An isolated render or screenshot without authored-source or project evidence is an image, not an activated visualisation situation.
Downloaded architectural references, precedent images and public render collections are consumed reference material.
A signed use schedule, approval, release or rights instrument standing alone remains protected evidence without copying creative facts into it.

sensitivity_why: Unreleased design intent, private client/site information, competition embargoes, security-sensitive views, source models, licensed textures or people/property imagery, approval contacts and use restrictions may be sensitive. The rule follows the evidenced packet and does not make every architectural image sensitive by extension or subject.
open_question: NJ-ARCHVIZ-1: Should a future creative schema expose a compact project/stage/artifact_type set that can hold scheme and view values, or should architectural visualisation remain a fieldless structural template? Recommended: preserve the fieldless placeholder until the schema decision is made. NJ-ARCHVIZ-2: When a visualisation is embedded in a planning or marketing submission, should the submission envelope and the source/render packet always co-hold, or should each remain separately activated by its own purpose evidence?
